issues.description: [suggestion] Surface synced sleep data as a Sleep card on Dashboard/Progress. issues.description: [suggestion] One-tap "Repeat meal" on the Nutrition diary — long-press or a small repeat-icon on any past meal card re-logs the same food(s)/quantities to today with one confirm tap, instead of requiring the CustomMealModal. Problem: athletes eat the same breakfast/post-workout shake most days but must reopen the manual-entry modal, hunt the food again via search or the buried "Recent meals" chip row (CustomMealModal.tsx:514-533), and resubmit every time — friction that discourages consistent logging (the exact behavior daily-completion/streak scoring depends on). Evidence: repo scan confirmed barcode scan, water tracker, and streak-freeze already exist, but no true repeat-log exists anywhere in src/pages/Nutrition.tsx or src/pages/_components/nutrition/ — the closest is the modal's prefill-only "Recent meals" row, which still requires opening the modal and resubmitting. Comparable trackers (MyFitnessPal "Copy meal", Cronometer "Copy from previous day") ship this as a core retention feature. v1 scope: add a repeat icon/swipe action on each meal-diary row (today or yesterday) that calls the existing add-meal/log endpoint with the same food_items + quantities, no new backend route needed; skip cross-day "copy whole day" for v1. Effort: ~0.5-1 day FE-only (new button + reuse existing log-meal service call).

issues.reviewReason: Root cause is a missing-asset problem, not a fixable frontend bug. AI-named plan exercises (e.g. 'Pec stretch in doorway', 'Overhead Arm Raise') have no image in the exercise catalog, so the card correctly shows the branded placeholder. The backend's only fallback is a loremflickr keyword URL, which the frontend intentionally blocks (BAD_IMAGE_HOSTS in src/lib/api-config.ts) because loremflickr returns wrong matches. I tested un-blocking loremflickr for exercises and captured the result: it returns irrelevant/duplicate stock photos (the SAME street-statue photo on 4 of 5 exercises) - clearly worse than the clean placeholder, so the block is protecting the premium look. Real exercise images need real demo assets populated in the catalog (backend/asset data-ops). Product call - which do you want: (a) invest in real exercise demo images (image worker / curated set), (b) keep the current clean placeholder, or (c) accept loremflickr stock photos despite the mismatches? No frontend-only change produces good images.
